title: windowed-reservation-reconciler-and-burst-leash
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see edge cases where short-term tenant bursts starve longer-running commitments because reservations are reconciled only at coarse intervals and burst credits are consumed without a soft leash. This change introduces a windowed reservation reconciler that reasons about recent allocation windows (sliding time buckets) and applies a configurable burst leash that gradually reduces burst allowance when a tenant's short-term consumption threatens group-level throughput guarantees.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a new reservation reconciler component (windowed_reservation_reconciler) that maintains lightweight sliding windows per-tenant and per-fleet partition. The reconciler exposes two knobs: window_length and decay_slope. The reconciler computes an expected committed utilization over the window, compares against contracted reservation and the fleet-level safety headroom, and emits soft adjustments to tenant burst allowances rather than hard preemption. To enforce fairness during contention, the reconciler introduces a burst_leash module that attaches to the existing credit bank and implements a slope-based reduction: when recent windowed utilization exceeds the committed percentile, burst allowance is reduced according to decay_slope over a configurable leash_duration. The leash is cooperative: it emits recommendations that the admission controller and slot allocator consume; hard enforcement happens only when safety thresholds are crossed.

Changes included: 1) runtime/controller: new sliding-window reconciler (go/service/reservation/windowed_reconciler.go) and unit tests; 2) controller API: new metrics and debug endpoint at /debug/reservations/windowed that returns LIS (list of compacted windows) and last action; 3) credit-bank: hooks to accept leash recommendations and apply soft caps for tentative allocations; 4) allocator: minor changes to accept tentative caps and prefer long-running reservations over recent bursts; 5) telemetry: new metrics (windowed_commit_pct, leash_invocations_total, leash_reduction_bytes) and dashboards + alert rule for leash_invocations spike; 6) integration tests: synthetic workload that reproduces the regression observed in ENG-1482; 7) docs: short design note in docs/ops/reservations.md.

Implementation notes: The reconciler keeps O(1) state per active tenant by compacting windows into 4-point summaries (count, sum, max, last_ts) to limit memory overhead. Window compaction and reconciliation run on a staggered schedule to avoid thundering herd. The leash uses a sigmoid-like clamp expressed as linear decay for simplicity and predictability; we can swap to a non-linear curve later if needed. All new knobs are feature-flagged behind ff.windowed_reservations to enable staged rollout to dedicated clusters.

Why this approach: We want to minimize hard preemptions and customer-visible failures while preserving hard throughput SLAs for committed tenants. The windowed approach captures recent bursty behavior without reacting to single-sample noise, and the leash provides a graceful, reversible lever for the allocator.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: Default behavior is unchanged when the feature flag is off. With the flag on, the reconciler defaults to conservative windows (60s) and gentle decay_slope (0.2) to avoid regressions. We added a smoke test to the deploy pipeline that flips the flag on a canary dedicated cluster and validates baseline throughput.

Benchmarks: In our synthetic scenario (50 tenants, 10% high-burst tenants), the reconciler reduced short-term SLA violations by ~72% with a 4.3% median increase in average latency for bursty requests (tradeoff due to soft-reductions). Memory overhead measured at +2.1MB per 1000 active tenants with compaction.

Security and cost: No new permissions. The debug endpoint is behind admin-only auth and respects audit logging. Additional metrics increase cardinality slightly; telemetry aggregator was updated to drop low-cardinality debug labels.

Open questions: whether to make leash curve configurable per-tenant and how this interacts with warm-pool warmups. A follow-up will add per-tenant profiles and a machine-learned slope suggestion service.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for reconciler logic - [x] Integration test reproducing ENG-1482 - [x] Telemetry + dashboard patch - [x] Docs note and rollout plan - [x] Feature-flag gating and smoke canary

References: ENG-1482 (regression), ENG-1560 (telemetry spike analysis), design doc /docs/design/windowed-reservations.md (attached).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we avoid adding per-tenant timers? Stagger reconciliation to a jittered cron or use the existing tick shard. Also please add memory accounting when compaction is enabled.
Maya Chen: Addressed by using the existing tick-shard and compacted 4-point summary; added mem accounting in windowed_reconciler.go and tests.
Lina Rodriguez: The leash feels too aggressive for small tenants that occasionally burst; can we make leash a function of reservation size (absolute) not just percentage?
Maya Chen: Updated algorithm to apply a min_absolute_threshold so leases don't reduce allowances below a small fixed byte/token floor for tiny reservations; updated tests and docs.
Noah Kim: CI integration test flakes on low-rps mode; I see a race in the test harness where the reconciler tick runs before synthetic traffic starts. Please add a warmup phase in the test.
Maya Chen: Added warmup phase to the integration test and a retry loop for the harness; flakiness gone in local runs.
Arjun Patel: Approve after minor nit on metric name (windowed_commit_pct -> windowed_commit_percentile).
Maya Chen: Renamed metric and updated dashboard and alert rule.

release_notes: Added windowed reservation reconciler and burst leash to reduce short-term SLA violations caused by bursty tenants. Feature gated and rolled out to canary Dedicated clusters. New telemetry: windowed_commit_percentile, leash_invocations_total, leash_reduction_bytes.
